channel.title: NBC Sports Fantasy Football News
channel.description: Latest player news and analysis for fantasy football from NBC Sports.

item.title: Rams placed Puka Nacua on injured reserve with knee and toe injuries.
item.description: Nacua will be eligible to return for the Rams’ Week 15 game against the Cowboys. The Rams are on bye in Week 11, and he is required to miss at least four games. It was previously reported that Nacua was expected to return in Week 14 or 15. Shortly before the team made this announcement, NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said that the team was “confident” Nacua would return in that timeframe. Rams coach Sean McVay previously said that the Rams would not place him on injured reserve due to transaction limitations. It is unclear whether anything has changed. Nacua suffered PCL and MCL sprains, along with a turf toe injury in Week 10 against the Commanders. ESPN’s Adam Schefter specifically cited Nacua’s MCL sprain after the move was made, adding that McVay said Nacua will miss “extended time.” Nacua should be stashed on fantasy football benches at this time.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Colby Parkinson (ribs) was limited on Thursday.
item.description: Parkinson should play through his injury again this week. Unfortunately, Tyler Higbee (illness) did not practice, as a new addition to the injury report, and Davis Allen (oblique) was downgraded to being a non-participant. The running backs are going to get all the work they can handle this week.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Trent McDuffie (back) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description: Earlier today, we were told that McDuffie would resume practicing today. It turns out that report was wrong. McDuffie is on the wrong side of questionable. Myles Garrett (knee) was limited. Steve Avila (hamstring) and Kam Curl (toe) did not practice.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Rashod Bateman (calf) was limited on Thursday.
item.description: The Ravens face the Chargers in Week 10’s Monday Night Football game, theoretically giving Bateman decent odds of suiting up. He does not need to be in starting lineups as a touchdown-dependent FLEX, though.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Vega Ioane (shoulder/knee) was limited on Thursday.
item.description: The Ravens’ stud rookie guard is on track to play this week, albeit with a new shoulder issue. Running backs Rasheen Ali (ankle) and Adam Randall (neck/hamstring) are practicing in full. They should play as well.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Bam Knight (concussion) practiced in full on Thursday.
item.description: Knight is on track to resume his lead rushing role this week. Unfortunately, the Cardinals face the Seahawks, potentially rendering Knight a touchdown-dependent FLEX starter against their elite defense. Hopefully, Knight remains setback-free for the rest of the week.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Deebo Samuel (hamstring) was limited on Thursday.
item.description: Samuel is still stuck in the questionable column, but his continued participation tentatively puts him on track to play in a fantasy-friendly matchup against the Cowboys in Week 10. If active, Samuel could end up serving as the 49ers’ No. 1 wide receiver. He would warrant WR3 treatment in this scenario.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Mike Evans (Achilles) will not practice on Thursday.
item.description: At this point, Evans seems like a long shot to play in Week 10 against the Cowboys. The 49ers allowed Christian McCaffrey to try to play through his Achilles tendinitis and it did not go well. 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan indicated they learned form the experience and will let Evans get fully healthy before allowing him to retake the field.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Charles Cross (ankle) resumed practicing on Thursday.
item.description: Cross and LB Uchenna Nwosu (ankle) were both limited at today’s practice, giving them a chance to play on Sunday against the Cardinals. Seahawks stud DT Leonard Williams (stinger) remains sidelined.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Drew Lock (elbow/oblique) was limited on Thursday.
item.description: Lock reportedly resumed throwing today, which is good to hear. He told reporters that the oblique injury is on the right side of his body, on the back of the muscle, which he thinks makes it easier to throw the football than when he had an oblique injury on the left side of his body two years ago. Lock is a QB2 this week against the Cardinals.-Nic Bodiford
